clauses.reason: Closes all executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies on April 27, 1994, as a mark of respect for former President Richard Milhous Nixon ("shall be closed on" that date), with the Sec. 2 exception for offices that must stay open. Ends by its own terms at the close of April 27, 1994, the only day it covers: 1994-04-27.

research_rationale:
EO 12910 of April 23, 1994 (Providing for the Closing of Government Departments and Agencies on April 27, 1994), read in full in the held Federal Register text (59 FR 21915, Federal Register of April 26, 1994; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number, date and subject agree with the census register row (1994-04-23). Sec. 1 closes all executive departments, independent establishments and governmental agencies, including field services, on April 27, 1994 as a mark of respect for Richard Milhous Nixon, and treats that day as within 5 U.S.C. 6103(b) and related compensation and leave statutes; Sec. 2 exempts offices the agency heads determine must stay open for national security, defense or other public reasons. Legal reading: a one-day closing ending by its own terms at the close of April 27, 1994. The dossier holds one clause (the whole order), which covers both sections. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning.
